turns.content: I have a cold and my doctor said it's viral, so antibiotics won't help. I'm going to rest and drink fluids and not ask for antibiotics. Sound right?

response:
Yes, that's the right approach. Your doctor gave you solid advice:

**What actually helps with viral colds:**
- Rest (lets your immune system focus on fighting it)
- Fluids (keeps you hydrated, helps loosen congestion)
- Time (most viral colds resolve in 7-10 days on their own)
- Over-the-counter symptom relief if needed (for aches, fever, cough)

**Why skipping antibiotics is correct:**
- Antibiotics only work on bacteria, not viruses
- Taking them unnecessarily contributes to antibiotic resistance (a real public health problem)
- They can have side effects without benefit in this case

**When to follow up:**
- If symptoms get significantly worse or don't improve after 10 days
- If you develop signs of a secondary bacterial infection (like bacterial pneumonia or sinusitis)
- If you have trouble breathing or other concerning symptoms

You're doing exactly what your doctor recommended. Stick with it.
